statements.quote: The next component of our long-term financial targets is driving Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 30-50 basis points annually. This equates to growing our margins by approximately 210 basis points from 2023 to 2028, reflecting Adjusted EBITDA margins of approximately 15% or $1.5 billion.
statements.speaker: Mark Witkowski

statements.quote: It's not a surprise at all for us to know that, you know, we've got annual goals that are higher than that 30-50 basis points that we laid out there. I'm very confident, given the levers that we've laid out and we've continued to execute against, that we can achieve those goals.

statements.quote: I think now it looks like you maybe need like 70 basis points of margin expansion per year to hit that number versus I think it was kind of 40-50 basis points per year at the time of the investor day and kind of the long-term annual value creation targets.

street.source: Baba data_financials consensus. Company fiscal years end about Feb 1, so company FY N = VA FY-(N+1): FY2026 = VA FY-2027, FY2028 = VA FY-2029 (EBITDA 1,100.2M on revenue 8,584.9M).

evidence_of_progress.note: Fiscal Q1 2026 (reported 2026-06-10): adjusted EBITDA margin up 10 bps to 11.8% (Robyn Bradbury, doc 6587). Fiscal Q2 2026 (reported 2026-09-09): up 10 bps to 12.8% (doc 219295). Fiscal 2025 full year was down 30 bps to 12.2% (doc 6588). Reaching 15% by fiscal 2028 from 12.2% needs about 93 bps a year; recent pace is about 10 bps.

verdict: Mechanically scores well (explicit 15% by fiscal 2028 target, consensus 218 bps short) but it is a stale 2023 target under an internal successor team whose change landed one day outside the window, margin already sits above the industry median, and progress runs at 10 bps a year, so this is a credibility gap more than a GXO-style inflection.
open_questions: Will management formally reset or reaffirm the 15% fiscal 2028 target (new investor day), given the needed pace is about 93 bps a year versus 10 bps delivered?
Does the April 2026 independent Chair and board refresh signal a strategy change, or only governance housekeeping after LeClair's exit?
Stage 1 shows CNM margin (12.3%) above the industry median (10.7%); is the peer set (Ferguson, Watsco, distributors) right for judging a below-peer margin gap?
